title: Hollow metal door frame in a stud or masonry wall

checklist.item: Frame anchors, their number per jamb and the wall framing they fix to are shown.
checklist.why: Loose frames are a hardware and fire-rating failure.

checklist.item: Fire-rated openings: frame label, wall rating, and grout or insulation fill as the listing requires are noted.
checklist.why: The rating of the opening must match the wall.

checklist.item: Exterior frames: head flashing with end dams, sealant at the perimeter, and a thermally broken or insulated frame.
checklist.why: Exterior hollow metal frames leak at the head and rust from inside.

checklist.item: Clear opening width and the door's maneuvering clearances are referenced.
checklist.why: The frame detail fixes the clear width.

checklist.item: Frame throat matches the wall thickness including finishes; the return on gypsum board is shown.
checklist.why: Wrong throat size is found when the frames arrive.

checklist.item: Bottom of frame at wet floors is held up or galvanized; silencers and hardware preparation are noted.
checklist.why: Frame feet rust at mopped floors.
